purpose: Machine-readable evidence map for the Hybrid Rewrite under NocoBase production-readiness audit.

requirements.statement: Django remains the source of truth; NocoBase is limited to low-risk admin/configuration surfaces.

patterns: Django backend remains the system of record
Do not do a full rebuild from scratch on NocoBase
Django remains the canonical backend and database owner

requirements.statement: First-release business decisions are locked in the core specification; remaining items are explicitly later scope, not implementation blockers.

patterns: The following decisions are fixed for the first production release
Expected first-release scale is about 600 clients total
Ops/admin users must be able to manage routine configuration without code
These still need to be decided before or during implementation planning

requirements.statement: NocoBase must not directly mutate payments, ledger, attendance, receipts, payroll calculations, or audit history; allowed config mutations must be audited in Django.

patterns: must not directly mutate payments, ledger, attendance, payroll calculations, receipts, or audit history
Never connect NocoBase direct SQL write access to payments, ledger, attendance, receipts, payroll calculations, or audit history

requirements.statement: The first NocoBase screens are defined by a build pack and validated against live Django bridge/config APIs.

NocoBase bootstrap and runtime startup use repository-pinned tooling plus production guards for secrets, default passwords, app root, storage, runtime fingerprinting, and health-checked background startup.

patterns: is required when NocoBase runs in production
NOCOBASE_APP_ROOT must be outside the source tree
NOCOBASE_STORAGE_DIR must be outside the source tree
NOCOBASE_APP_KEY must be a real production secret at least 32 characters long
NocoBase production app key strength guard passed
NocoBase production root password strength guard passed

requirements.statement: Archived participants remain visible for history, but cannot receive new operational, scheduling, billing, or subscription actions.
Parents can see only their own children and cannot upload receipts for another account.

patterns: A parent can see only their own children

requirements.statement: Trainers cannot see client financial data and can only operate on their own sessions.
Only confirmed payments affect balances, reports, and debt calculations.
Payment method is required and supports cash plus bank transfer/internal transfer records.
Charge and payment records are retained; receipt files may be purged but financial history remains.

patterns: Charge history is immutable and cannot be deleted.

requirements.statement: Subscriptions stay valid through end date plus 7 days, and admins can manually adjust remaining sessions while operational subscription, ledger, and freeze history cannot be deleted outside guarded import rollback.

patterns: Admin can manually adjust the remaining number of sessions
Manual adjustments must remain in history

requirements.statement: Scheduling supports reschedules/transfers, trainer substitutions, and group/individual/split session types.
Admins can manage per-session waitlists, promote students into the concrete roster, and keep waitlist history.
Attendance is auditable, affects session ledger correctly, and attendance history must not be deleted.

patterns: Attendance history must never be deleted

requirements.statement: Quiet hours are configurable; due messages are not sent at night and are deferred to the nearest allowed time.
Notification templates and delivery rendering support multiple languages.
Admin can configure payroll rules by session type, including group thresholds, extra clients, individual, and split sessions.

patterns: Group payroll is based on held sessions and client count above a minimum
Individual sessions use a fixed amount per session
Split sessions use a separate fixed amount per session

requirements.statement: System supports multiple locations, multilingual UI/templates, and localizable reference dictionaries.
Ops/admin users can run debt/upcoming/income reports and export operational data without direct database access.

patterns: ops/admin can run reporting and routine maintenance safely

requirements.statement: Admin can export complete client data for access requests and anonymize client accounts through audited backend flows.

patterns: implement client data export for sensitive-data workflows

requirements.statement: Financial and sensitive actions are audited, emitted to server logs, and protected from audit-log tampering.
Production rejects unsafe settings such as DEBUG enabled, wildcard hosts, weak secrets, source-tree runtime paths, and missing HTTPS reverse-proxy settings.
A repeatable full-stack release gate validates backend, NocoBase, frontend build, dependency audit, smoke tests, and CI workflow structure.

required release manifest is not tracked by git
operator checklist covers every external action
working tree is not clean, so a release source archive cannot be built
must stop if evidence is missing

requirements.statement: CI includes a PostgreSQL backend test job so production database behavior is verified separately from SQLite convenience tests.

patterns: Python setup before tracked manifest check

requirements.statement: Production operations include hybrid backup, checksum-guarded restore, and live health checks for Django, NocoBase bridge/config APIs, and the NocoBase process.

environment must be 'production' for cutover approval

evidence must include current release archive sha256

requirements.statement: Readiness and ops endpoints expose backend health, NocoBase blueprint/build-pack status, and operational backlog.
Frontend production build and basic accessibility smoke are part of the release gate.
